audit.title: Policy Ordering and Composition
audit.summary: This is a well-written conceptual page explaining how Chainlink ACE policy chains execute and how ordering affects security. Its biggest strength is clean, answer-first prose with crisp verbatim-liftable definitions (Reject/Allow/Continue, terminal outcomes, default result). Its biggest opportunity is machine-readability: no JSON-LD, no canonical URL, and — most damaging — the three diagrams that carry the core teaching content render as "(Image: Image)" with no alt text or captions, so an engine loses the visual reasoning entirely. Structuring the outcome and default-result facts into tables and adding symptom-phrased headings would raise both extraction and retrieval.

recommendations.title: Add alt text / captions to the three diagrams
recommendations.where: "Ordering example" (Ordering A, Ordering B images) and "How the engine evaluates a chain" (sequence diagram)
recommendations.issue: all three render as `(Image: Image)` with no text equivalent
recommendations.change: add descriptive captions/alt text spelling out each diagram's flow, e.g. "Sequence: PolicyEngine runs extractors once, then evaluates each policy in order; first Reject reverts, first Allow approves and skips the rest, Continue defers." The sequence-diagram content has no textual equivalent anywhere on the page.
recommendations.why: engines cannot read raster diagrams; the core evaluation model is currently unretrievable except from prose fragments.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased heading for the default-result failure mode
recommendations.issue: the failure ("your transactions will revert unexpectedly") is buried in body text, not a heading
recommendations.change: add an H3 such as "Why do my transactions revert when all policies return Continue?" and answer in the first sentence (default result set to reject).
recommendations.why: devs/agents query by symptom; a question-phrased heading wins retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Convert the three outcomes and default-result options to tables
recommendations.issue: decision-critical data is in bullet prose; 0 tables on page
recommendations.change: a 3-row Outcome | Return value | Effect on chain table, and a 2-row `desired_default_allow` | Behavior | When to use table.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract reasons and build justified comparative answers.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: measured facts show 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified in head
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2026-03-31` (already in body), and a canonical `<link>`; expose the last-updated date as visible HTML too.
recommendations.why: structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent parse-trust; low effort, site-template-level.

recommendations.title: Add concrete gas/positioning specifics
recommendations.issue: "each policy in the chain costs gas" — no figures
recommendations.change: give an order-of-magnitude per-policy gas overhead or state that extractors run once regardless of chain length with a concrete cost example, if available.
recommendations.why: quantitative claims are among the highest-lift additions; qualitative-only prose underperforms.

recommendations.title: Add a short config snippet for `desired_default_allow`
recommendations.issue: field named but never shown in a settable form (0 code blocks on page)
recommendations.change: add a small labeled snippet or API/UI call showing where `desired_default_allow` is set per target contract.
recommendations.why: an agent completing a config task needs a copy-pasteable form of the field, not prose.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifier "most" in "the most common approach for composable policy chains" — acceptable but could be quantified or softened.
Images with no alt text / captions (also captured under P1) — content loss for non-visual consumers.
No stale-content or fluff issues; prose is clean and undated-in-head only (body carries the date).
offPageNotes: The page references `/llms.txt` — good site-level signal; ensure it lists this URL.
Canonical URL and JSON-LD are likely template/site-level concerns rather than author-editable; flag to the docs platform team.
CLI did not capture `<head>` — pass raw head HTML for a definitive metadata read; the body-level "Last Updated" suggests dates may exist but aren't machine-exposed.
